reconcile.note: Matthew Henry defines Asa's perfect heart as sincere devotion rather than sinlessness, a standard his later failures do not overturn.

discrepancy.emptyNote: 1 Kings 15:14 says Asa's heart was perfect with Yahweh all his days, while 2 Chronicles 16:7 has a prophet rebuke Asa for relying on the king of Syria rather than Yahweh.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Editorial statement of the mechanism; catalogued by Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Was Asa Perfect?") (2013).

sides.snippet: the heart of Asa was perfect with Yahweh all his days
sides.verseText: But the high places were not taken away: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with Yahweh all his days.

sides.snippet: Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on Yahweh your God
sides.verseText: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said to him, Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on Yahweh your God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of your hand.
